headline: Obesity-drug surge funds a guidance raise and dealmaking
summary_short: Lilly's Q2 2026 revenue rose 48% to $23.0 billion on Mounjaro and Zepbound volume, with reported EPS up 26% to $7.94 despite $3.03/share of acquired IPR&D charges; the company raised full-year revenue guidance to $85.0-$87.0 billion.
summary_long: Volume grew 60% y/y, offset by a 13% price decline; Mounjaro (+91% to $9.9B) and Zepbound (+46% to $4.9B, U.S.) led growth. Gross margin rose to 85.8% of revenue (+150bp) on lower production cost and mix. Net income and EPS were held back by $2.8B of acquired IPR&D charges (Orna, Ajax, Centessa, Kelonia), $703M of special charges, and a higher tax rate (23.3% vs 16.5%). Lilly raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $85.0-$87.0B (from $82-$85B) and margin guidance to 49.0-50.5%; non-GAAP EPS guidance's ceiling fell to $36.50 (from $37.00) as a $2.78 underlying raise was more than offset by $3.03 of new IPR&D charges. Cash rose to $8.95B; long-term debt rose to $47.86B, funding the deals and a $4.5B Indiana commitment.

drivers.explanation: Driven primarily by Mounjaro and Zepbound volume; worldwide volume +60% y/y, partially offset by a 13% decline in realized prices. U.S. revenue +33%, ex-U.S. revenue +80% (helped by a $250M Jardiance milestone).
Higher net income drove the increase, but $3.03/share of acquired IPR&D charges (vs $0.14 a year ago) muted growth relative to the underlying business improvement.

Higher gross margin and revenue were partly offset by $2.8B of acquired IPR&D charges (mainly Orna and Ajax), $703M of special charges tied to the Kelonia/Centessa deals, and a higher effective tax rate (23.3% vs 16.5%) from non-deductible IPR&D costs.
Gross margin rose to 85.8% of revenue (+150bp y/y) on improved cost of production and favorable product mix, partially offset by lower realized prices.
